issues.description: The problem statement and the template define Developer.monthsOfSwiftExperience as an Optional Int (Int?), but the solution implementation uses an Optional Double (Double?) for the same property. This type mismatch across artifacts is structural and can confuse students about the correct type to use and how to implement conditional logic (optional binding, switch on value, and incrementing).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent. Preferably change the solution to use Int? for monthsOfSwiftExperience (matching the problem statement and template) and update the solution's initializer, swiftExperienceDescription(), and attend(course:) to work with Int (e.g., switch on Int value, increment by 1). Alternatively, if Double is intentional, update the problem statement and template to specify Double?.

issues.description: The property monthsOfSwiftExperience is described in the problem statement and declared in the template as type Int? but the solution implementation uses the same identifier monthsOfSwiftExperience with type Double?. This mismatch (same conceptual property, different concrete type) breaks the expected mapping between the specification and the reference solution and may confuse students about the expected type and how to implement increments and switch comparisons.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of monthsOfSwiftExperience consistent across artifacts. Prefer aligning the solution with the problem/template by changing monthsOfSwiftExperience in the solution from Double? to Int? and update any related logic (switch and increment) to use Int arithmetic. Alternatively, if Double is intentional, update the problem statement and template to specify Double? and adjust examples accordingly.
